Release path

Build the small combat loop before scaling to squads and online runs.

Game systems

The rules that connect programming, combat, and rewards.

01 / Program

Prompt-to-plan tactics

Android runs Qwen2.5 locally; USB computer tests use Qwen3.5. A shared squad script handles formations and target orders. Compile adds a validated tactical stance; the script also works without a model.

02 / Commands

Unit programming language

Radar, Gun, Drive, Duck, Cover, and Sniper Perch are program commands. They grant actions and conditions without changing the natural-language instruction. Future unit types can have their own command sets.

03 / Fight

Multi-domain units

Play tanks, infantry, helicopters, rocket soldiers, artillery and snipers in squad battles. Collect recruits from victories and combine three matching units to unlock commands. Deploy squads of up to 15, add coastal boats, or create an invite match.

04 / Reward

Instructions earned by winning

Victory currently offers an instruction and a buff that lasts one round. Future local-model generation and roguelite progression will expand the choices.

05 / Balance

36 distinct stats

Offense, weapon handling, defense, mobility, sensing, and utility each affect a different mechanic. Numbers remain visible on tank cards so players can understand why a tactic worked.

06 / Later

Long-term collection

The game now includes real 3D graphics, drag-and-drop inventory, broad weapon and armor selection, three-of-a-kind unit upgrades, and cosmetics earned by retiring tanks. Retirement counts at most five wins per tank.
